item.title: Air Attack Sets Fuel Depot Ablaze at Airport in Saudi Capital
item.description: The assault came as the kingdom has been targeted by Yemen’s Houthi rebels and by drones from Iraq.

item.title: The Twin Sisters Facing the Wrath of Iran’s Crackdown
item.description: Romina and Taraneh Rahimi were detained in January after a wave of protests. One was sentenced to decades behind bars; the other was condemned to death.

item.title: Germany’s Military Rebuild Is Making Its Neighbors Nervous
item.description: The country’s fast-paced rearmament is rekindling a century-old debate about how much hard power Berlin should have.

item.title: Inside Machado’s Plan to Return to Venezuela and Revive Its Democracy
item.description: The Nobel laureate is planning her comeback from exile in Panama, setting up a clash with the U.S.-backed interim government.

item.title: U.S. Reaches Greenland Security Agreement
item.description: The deal, which will enhance American military presence on the Arctic island, falls short of the president’s stated takeover ambitions.

item.title: Xi Jinping Skipped One Dinner—and Sparked a Flurry of Questions About His Health
item.description: The Chinese leader felt unwell at the recent Brics event in India, reviving worries over who would succeed him.

item.title: Donald Trump Jr. Repaid Russian Businessman Who Funded Wedding Afterparty, President Says
item.description: The two-day post-wedding celebrations in the Bahamas were financed by Umar Kremlev, a businessman with ties to Russian President Putin.

item.title: Oil Futures Fall for Third Day on Easing Supply Concerns
item.description: Oil futures fell, with market concerns about Saudi Arabia supply disruptions tempered by expectations that some flows could soon be restored through the kingdom’s damaged East-West Pipeline.

item.title: Canada Ready to Clawback Stellantis Cash Unless Production Resumes at Toronto-Area Factory
item.description: The plant, in Brampton, Ontario, has been idle since 2024, and Stelantis is in advanced talks to sell that factory to a Canadian armored-car maker.

item.title: Why Russia Is Holding an Election When Voters Know the Result
item.description: The election is meant to jump-start flagging support for President Vladimir Putin and the war.

item.title: Multibillion-Dollar Stock-Market Scandal Roils Erdogan’s Turkey
item.description: The implosion of a series of investment funds that held billions of dollars heaped fresh stress on Turkey’s troubled economy.

item.title: Hundreds of Thousands Rally in Iran as War and Economy Squeeze
item.description: The pro-government push comes as Iran faces economic woes in the U.S. blockade and an anniversary of the 2022 protests.

item.title: Russia Seizes Control of Nestlé’s Local Operations
item.description: Russia also placed the local businesses of French retailers Auchan and Leroy Merlin under temporary external administration, according to a presidential decree.

item.title: Bank of Japan Raises Rates, Making U.S. Less Alluring for Tokyo Investors
item.description: The yen weakened as two members of the bank’s board suggested future rate rises might come more slowly than anticipated.

item.title: Malaysia’s Former Prime Minister Can Serve Rest of 1MDB Sentence Under House Arrest
item.description: The royal pardon for Najib Razak marks the latest chapter in one of the largest financial crimes of the century.

item.title: North Korea Sends Women to Russian Factories in Line of Ukrainian Fire
item.description: Kim Jong Un has deployed factory crews into an expanding war zone to bolster ties with President Vladimir Putin.

item.title: The U.S. and China Want AI Guardrails. But Their Ideas Couldn’t Be More Different.
item.description: American dialogue has centered on protecting humanity from the technology, while Beijing is chiefly concerned with safeguarding the Communist Party.

item.title: Stellantis Could Face Strike Threat in Canada Over Factory Sale
item.description: The union representing more than 9,000 Stellantis employees in Canada said it could be in a strike position in the coming weeks unless the carmaker changes course on its plan to sell a Toronto-area factory to a defense firm.

item.title: Crude Oil Futures Post Back-to Back Losses
item.description: Oil prices fell amid expectations that Saudi Arabia could soon restore some oil flows through its damaged East-West pipeline while shipping crude through the Strait of Hormuz.
